svg.text: Two Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040) boards · I²C tester-to-sensor wiring
Original Raspberry Pi Pico (not Pico W) · top / component view · both micro-USB sockets point UP
STOP — UNPLUG BOTH USB CABLES BEFORE YOU CONNECT ANYTHING.
Keep BOTH boards unplugged until every wire and both resistors have been checked. Each board is then powered only by its own USB cable.
Both boards seen from above, USB at the top. 40 pads each.
R1 from TESTER pin 36 to the SDA
R2 from TESTER pin 36 to the SCL
Check with a meter, then plug both
solder pad / hole (physical pin number in the dark box)
coloured ring = pin used in this wiring
✕ = pin 36 on SENSOR must stay EMPTY
Pin numbers are not printed on a real Pico: pin 1 is the top-left pad at the USB end. Count 1→20 down the left side, then 21→40 up the right side.
Electrical view — wire length and physical routing are not to scale.
Both resistors start at the same point: TESTER pin 36 (3V3 OUT).
That pin supplies ONLY the pull-ups. One resistor's free end goes to the SDA wire, the other's to the SCL wire —
separately. The resistors are not in series with the board-to-board wires, and the SENSOR's pin 36 is never connected to anything.
Resistor orientation does not matter (5.1 kΩ is not polarised). Wire colours are arbitrary — pick your own and stay consistent.
pin 6 ↔ pin 6, pin 7 ↔ pin 7, pin 8 ↔ pin 8 all beep (≈0 Ω).
Leave SENSOR pin 36 and both boards' pins 39/40 unwired.
Each ≈5.1 kΩ before fitting. Connected boards can alter readings.
VBUS (40) and VSYS (39) are not used. Only 3V3(OUT) feeds the resistors.
GP4→GP4, GP5→GP5. Swapping SDA and SCL will simply not communicate.
Join VBUS, VSYS, 3V3_EN, RUN or SWD between boards.
Connect SENSOR pin 36. This diagram uses TESTER pin 36 only.
Add a 5 V wire. Neither board needs one and it can destroy an input.
I²C is bidirectional — both boards drive SDA.
The TESTER makes the clock and starts each transfer, but the SENSOR also
pulls SDA low to acknowledge bytes and to send its replies. Never let both
boards act as bus master at the same time.
Pinout verified against Raspberry Pi Ltd: Pico datasheet RP-008307-DS §2.1 and the official “Raspberry Pi Pico Pinout” poster
Illustrative diagram, not a breadboard layout and not to scale. No hardware was connected or powered to make it.
